title: Year four close: the many rooms
hook: thinkers, prayers, ethics, hope and the hardest questions: one house with many rooms (John 14:2)
tomorrow: Four women in the family tree (Matthew 1:1–17)

segments.voice: Yesterday, faith as faithfulness: Daniel at his open window, praying as he did aforetime. Your line was keep showing up.

At the table on Jesus' last night, one of his friends admits he's lost. Jesus has just told them not to be troubled, and that he is going to prepare a place for them. Thomas doesn't nod along: "Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?" This year opened with the promise Thomas was answering, about a house with many rooms. Today the year closes in the same room, with the same line, and Thomas's question still on the table.

John's Gospel, in the King James: "In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you." This year walked that house room by room. The big questions, each church answering in its own voice. Prayer, from the Jesus Prayer to Quaker silence to a hymn. Ethics: commandments, virtues and mercy. The great thinkers, arguing across the centuries. Revelation and Christian hope, from a garden to a garden-city. Church life: rites and spaces, bells and bread. And these last weeks, the hardest room: suffering, doubt, grief, and love that walks into pain without explaining it. Now notice who first heard many mansions. Frightened friends. Peter, just told he would deny Jesus before the rooster crowed. Thomas, saying out loud that he didn't know the way. Right after Peter hears that, Jesus says: "Let not your heart be troubled." And then: "I go to prepare a place for you." A place prepared for them as they are: troubled, unsure, about to fail. Christians read the line in more than one way: some hear it about heaven, some about the church on earth, some about life with God that starts now, and some readers hold those side by side. But in the story, the promise of a room comes before the confusion is cleared up. Thomas asks his question, and what he hears next is an answer, not a rebuke.

segments.voice: Walk back through the year's rooms in your mind and notice which one you kept returning to and which one you're standing in today. It might be the room of doubt, with Thomas; that's a room in the house, too. Let one line form, I live in the room of, and finish it yourself; if you pray, offer it to God as it is.
Year four close. The last day of a year spent in one house with many rooms: thinkers, prayer, ethics, hope and the hardest questions. A house first promised to friends who were afraid.
Your line: there is room for you. Tomorrow, year five opens on the first page of Matthew. See you there.

chat.says: Jesus promised his friends a place. Weren't they the ones who had it all figured out?
options: No. He said it to frightened friends: Peter about to deny him, Thomas unsure of the way.
Yes. The promise came only after Thomas stopped asking and finally understood the way.
Yes. He said it at a joyful feast after Easter, once all their doubts were gone.
chat.meaning: In John 14, the promise of a room came to troubled friends, before their confusion was cleared up. Thomas's question got an answer, not a rebuke.

many mansions.meaning: dwelling places, rooms to stay in, in one house
